questions.prompt: What does a language model fundamentally do with your prompt?

options.text: Looks up the answer in a database of verified facts
Predicts the next token again and again, continuing the text in the way that best fits what it sees
Runs a search engine query and copies the top result
Translates the prompt into code and executes it

questions.explanation: A model generates one token at a time, each time predicting what best continues everything it has seen so far. That's why changing what it sees changes what it writes.

questions.prompt: Which of these can be part of a prompt? Select all that apply.

options.text: Background context the model can't know
Examples of the output you want

questions.explanation: A prompt holds instructions, context, input data, examples, and format guidance. The model's weights are fixed by training and aren't part of a prompt.

questions.prompt: Small chunks of text, such as whole words, parts of words, or punctuation, that a model reads and writes are called ____.
questions.explanation: Text is split into tokens before the model reads it, and the model generates its answer one token at a time.

questions.prompt: A model without web access is asked for this morning's top news. What's the best fix?

options.text: Ask the same question five more times
Use a tool with web search, or paste the articles and ask for a summary of those
Ask the model to pretend it has internet access

questions.explanation: Prompting can't add knowledge the model lacks. Supply the information yourself or connect a tool that can fetch it.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of the prompt engineering loop in order.

items.text: Test the prompt on real inputs
Design a prompt with task, context, and format
Save the version that works and note why
Refine one thing at a time
Inspect the output against what you wanted

questions.explanation: Good prompts come from a loop: design, test, inspect, refine (one change per round), then save what works.

questions.prompt: Match each lever to the situation it fits best.

pairs.right: Always the first thing to try
A narrow behavior needed at very large scale

questions.explanation: Prompting is free and instant, retrieval brings in large or changing documents, tools fetch live data or compute exactly, and fine-tuning changes default behavior at scale.
